# Lane 2.238: the independent review (2026-11-26)

Tried on the real PostgreSQL 16.15 of this machine (`node scripts/real-postgres.mjs start`, then `stop`), 30 plants by the tables' owner in a throwaway test, each checked with `checkLoginRole` and, where it matters, read AS `app_login` with league A set. The test is not committed.

## Findings

- **High: a renamed league column hides the table from the whole guard.** `packages/database/src/db/fence-catalog.ts` lines 42-49 find a league table only by a column named `league_id` (or a foreign key target). See it: `alter table public.activity_log rename column league_id to lg`, then `create policy w on public.activity_log for select using (true)` (or `disable row level security`): the guard says nothing, and app_login reads both leagues' rows. (`programs` stays seen only because other tables point at it.) Mend: write the league tables' names into `migration-catalog.ts` and hold every listed one, whatever its columns, as well as any found.
- **High: a view or materialized view in a schema no migration made reads past the fence unseen.** `check-fence.ts` lines 165-176 and T-471 read only the migrations' five schemas. See it: `create schema x; create view x.p as select * from public.programs; grant usage on schema x, select on x.p to app_login`: silent, app_login sees both leagues (same for a materialized view, and for `create table x.c as select league_id as lg, name from public.programs`). In `public` the same view is refused. Mend: in every schema, refuse a view or materialized view that depends on a league table (`pg_depend` through `pg_rewrite`) and is not in the catalog, or read (d) in every schema but a pinned list of the hosted service's own.
- **High: a reviewed security-definer function's body can be changed by hand unseen.** `check-fence.ts` line 137 and `reviewed-definers.ts` line 13 key on the signature only. See it: `create or replace function public.find_league_by_slug(wanted text)` with the `where` clauses removed: the guard is silent, and app_login gets all 4 leagues from `find_league_by_slug('no-such-slug')`. Mend: put a hash of each reviewed function's `prosrc`, `proconfig` and owner from the fresh run into the catalog and refuse a difference.
- **Medium: a correctly migrated hosted database is not yet shown to pass.** On this server a fresh database at the same 30 migrations passes (the guard returned nothing before and after every plant), and the step adds no migration, so a database made before this step at those migrations holds the same catalog (the runner pins each migration's checksum). Not shown: the test copy's Supabase schemas (their definer functions keep PUBLIC's EXECUTE unless revoked, and the guard would name each) and a server version other than 16 and 17. If either differs, the website's or the worker's start on the test copy stops. No live site runs this guard today (the tracker in `apps/live-stats` does not call `checkLoginRole`). Mend: the founder-session start against the test copy that builder 2 asked for, before any real league's data.
- **Low: three of the policy comparisons are tested by nothing.** `check-fence.ts` lines 79-81. Break: `found.roles === made.roles` replaced by `true`: all 13 real-server tests in `tests/real-postgres/fence-guard.test.ts` and all 13 in `check-fence.test.ts` still pass (put back). A roles-only change narrows rather than widens today, so Low. Mend: one plant `alter policy programs_league_fence on public.programs to app_user`, and one each for command and permissive.
- **Low: in `fence-guard.test.ts` lines 56-57 an undo that throws inside `finally` replaces the first failure's message.** The test still fails, but names the wrong cause. Mend: collect undo errors and throw them after.
- **Low: `sign_in.users ... no force row level security` is not seen.** Not a league table, so outside the promise; note it in T-471.

## The ten items

1. Permissive policy beside the right one: refused, and it was real (login saw both leagues).
2. Same-named policy `for select` only, `to` a role the login may become, `league_id = league_id`, `... or true`: each refused. No migration policy is restrictive; a dropped fence policy denies everything (login saw no rows).
3. View in a new schema: got through. Materialized view in a new schema: got through. View in `public`: refused. Inheriting table and partition (new schema): refused by (a).
4. Definer through login, A, B (inherit, and set-only): refused. PUBLIC's EXECUTE granted: refused. Same name, other arguments or schema: not runnable (migration 0005 revokes PUBLIC's default), refused once granted; the list keys schema, name and arguments. Body changed: got through.
5. BYPASSRLS through a role: refused. A table owned through a role: refused. Fence off in another schema: refused. Column renamed: got through.
6. Catalog stale: not silent; deleting one line made `migration-catalog-file.test.ts` fail, and at start a new table would be refused by (d). Created-then-dropped tables cannot confuse it (it reads a fresh run's end state). Guard time on the real server: 8 to 30 ms per call.
7. `my_leagues`: true (owner, live grant or roster place of the account set, nothing for none). `take_jobs`: true (ids and lease only, refused with a league or account set), but the website's login may call it too, not only the worker. `account_for_sign_in`: true that it reads no league table, but builder 1 is right to be uneasy: any app_login session can link an unlinked account, by email, to any sign-in id; the fence is not crossed, an account is.
8. Exact-sentence checks (`toEqual`) cannot pass on a different refusal; a dead server throws. The roles break above passed every test.
9. T-468 and T-470: the catalog records names and rules but not function bodies or which tables are league tables (Highs 1 and 3). T-471: the five-schema limit is the view leak (High 2). T-469 (trigger functions left out): sound, since attaching one needs the owner.
10. See the Medium above: passes at the same migrations here; the test copy itself is unverified.
